title: Workbench
brief: Workbench is Gusto’s internal design system — React components, colors, typography, patterns, and all the visual assets common to Gusto’s brand. I was part of the team of designers and engineers who planned and built it from scratch. I built and owned the documentation site itself — which was formerly public, though it’s now internal-only — as the source of truth for the system, with extensive documentation for Gusto’s ~500 designers and engineers, including a monthly newsletter.
scope: System work: research → API design → accessibility → build. Documentation site: most of the design → content writing → build → deploy.

images.caption: Introduces the system through tailored onboarding for designers (Figma) and engineers (code), supported by Loom video walkthroughs.
An extensive library of React components was built collaboratively by design and engineering to ensure accessibility, responsiveness, and performance.

images.caption: Component documentation includes anatomy graphics — form fields, in this example — to establish a shared design and engineering vocabulary.

title: James Button Oboe
summary: A personal website for a classical oboe musician.
brief: A web presence for San Francisco Symphony’s Associate Principal Oboist to establish a brand and to promote audition coaching and guest performance work. The color palette is largely drawn from sampling the hero image and features high-legibility typography, an integrated event calendar, and a custom audio player for his excerpts.
scope: Full scope: Design, UX, content strategy, technical SEO → build → launch.
status: Live and actively driving client referrals.

images.alt: Audio excerpts page with custom audio player
images.caption: A custom, lightweight audio player built for playing performance excerpts.

images.alt: Events calendar page for James Button Oboe
images.caption: Upcoming special event listings are powered dynamically by Sanity CMS.

title: The Beeline
summary: A showcase of road biking routes in San Francisco.
brief: A streamlined, app-style cycling dashboard built for SF-based riders to filter and explore favorite routes without marketing clutter or unnecessary link-drilling. The name Beeline was inspired by the winding trail a bee leaves looping through the air — similar to the way bike routes weave around the Bay Area. The bold, playful design references the colors of a bee.
scope: Full scope: Design, content → build → launch.
status: v1 is live. Next phase: re-riding routes to catalog explicit points of interest like water stops, lunch spots, and viewpoints.

title: Tails
summary: A digital library of my personal cocktail collection.
brief: A clean, ad-free mobile cocktail recipe catalog designed to keep focus on drink preparation rather than dismissing popups. I call it Tails, as in cocktails (hold for applause). There’s relatively little interactivity, so React — and by extension, Next.js — felt like overkill, so I built it in Astro instead.
scope: Full scope: Design, content → build → launch.
status: v1 is live. Planned enhancements: search functionality, favorites, and further mobile UI polish.
